hero.title: Questions people ask before they start
hero.body: Straight answers about language, cost, storage and safety — the things people usually want to know first.

one.question: Is Mero Health available in Nepali?
one.answer: Yes. Nepali is the default language across the site and the assistant; switch to English at any time from the language toggle.

two.question: Do I need health insurance to use it?
two.answer: No. You can create an account and start on the free plan directly, without an insurer, referral or employer plan.

three.question: Where is my health record stored?
three.answer: Wherever you choose — your own Google Drive, kept client-encrypted so only you can read it, or Mero Health's hosted storage. You can change this later.

four.question: Can the assistant handle a medical emergency?
four.answer: The assistant does not diagnose. A deterministic safety check runs before every answer, and anything that looks like an emergency is intercepted first and pointed to appropriate care.

five.question: Does the assistant read everything I upload automatically?
five.answer: Extraction produces a draft first. Only observations you've confirmed or corrected are ever used by the assistant, a share link or an export — a draft never reaches any of those on its own.

six.question: What if the free plan isn't enough?
six.answer: Add hosted storage, automatic document extraction, device sync or clinician consultations as separate modules whenever you need them — an upgrade only adds what you choose.

dataConsent.guide: Nothing below is used for a purpose while it's off. You can turn any of these off again at any time, and the app's core service works the same either way.

modelTrainingText.title: Written messages — to improve the Nepali assistant
modelTrainingText.body: Messages you write, after clear identifiers like phone numbers and emails are automatically removed, may be used to train the Nepali health assistant. Because things like names or places can still remain, anything that might identify you is checked by a person before it is used.

modelTrainingVoice.title: Voice — a separate permission
modelTrainingVoice.body: The same purpose as written messages, but for the text transcribed from your voice, not the recording itself. Because voice is more identifying, every voice sample is always checked by a person before use — not only sometimes, the way written messages are.

humanReview.title: Human review
humanReview.body: Someone at Mero Health may read your de-identified conversation — to check quality, or before it is used for the purposes above. If this is off, anything that might identify you is never used.

storageChoice.title: Choosing where your record lives
storageChoice.summary: Your own Google Drive or Mero Health's hosted storage — both are your choice, and you can change it later.

body.paragraphOne: Every document you capture ends up in one of two places: your own Google Drive, or Mero Health's hosted storage. Google Drive stays entirely yours — the file is encrypted on your device before it ever leaves it, so it's opaque to anyone but you, including Mero Health.
body.paragraphTwo: Hosted storage is where extraction, search and sharing are offered as part of the product, which is why it's a separate paid module rather than the default. Either way, the choice is yours, and you can change it later.

relatedPrompt.heading: See the full picture
relatedPrompt.body: This is one of three principles behind how Mero Health handles your data — see all three on the Privacy page.

confirmedRecords.title: Why nothing is used until you confirm it
confirmedRecords.summary: Extraction from an uploaded document produces a draft first — only what you confirm or correct is ever used.

body.paragraphOne: When you upload a lab report or prescription, the first thing that happens is extraction — turning a photograph into structured values. That result is a draft, not a fact. It sits in a queue for you to review.
body.paragraphTwo: Only after you confirm a value, or correct it, does it become part of your record — something the assistant can reason over, a share link can include, or an export can contain. A draft never reaches any of those on its own; the confirmation step is not optional and cannot be skipped.

relatedPrompt.heading: More questions like this
relatedPrompt.body: This is one of the questions people ask most before they start — see the rest on the FAQ page.

safetyCheck.title: The safety check that runs before every answer
safetyCheck.summary: A deterministic check, independent of the language model, runs ahead of every assistant response — and it doesn't diagnose.

body.paragraphOne: Before the assistant's response ever reaches you, a separate, deterministic check runs first — rules, not a language model, deciding whether what's about to be shown needs to be intercepted. This runs on every single response, not just the ones that look risky in hindsight.
body.paragraphTwo: If anything looks like it could be a medical emergency, that check catches it before the model's answer is shown, and points you to appropriate care instead. The assistant itself does not diagnose — its job is to help you understand your own record, not to replace a clinician.

relatedPrompt.heading: How we think about quality
relatedPrompt.body: This safety check is one part of how Mero Health approaches clinical quality — read more on the Commitment to Quality page.
